chunks.title: ISI Mark - Product Certification (Scheme-I): Find the Indian Standard for your product
chunks.body: Search for the Indian Standard against the product using the Application/Licence-related search on MANAK Online; if it cannot be found, send a query to the concerned BIS technical department.

chunks.title: ISI Mark - Product Certification (Scheme-I): Submit application online on MANAK Online
chunks.body: BIS accepts product certification applications, including all payments, in online mode only, through the www.manakonline.in portal. Fee: Application fee: Rs. 1,000 (non-refundable)

chunks.title: ISI Mark - Product Certification (Scheme-I): BIS preliminary inspection visit
chunks.body: BIS carries out an assessment of the manufacturing infrastructure, process controls, quality control and testing capability through a visit to the factory premises. Fee: Inspection fee: Rs. 7,000 per man-day, payable before the preliminary inspection visit

chunks.title: ISI Mark - Product Certification (Scheme-I): Conformity testing of the product
chunks.body: Conformity to the relevant Indian Standard is established either through third-party laboratory testing, testing in the manufacturer's own premises, or a combination of both. Under Option-2, only test reports from BIS, or a BIS-recognised/empanelled laboratory, are acceptable, and must generally not be more than 90 days old.

chunks.title: ISI Mark - Product Certification (Scheme-I): Licence granted and marking/annual fee deposited
chunks.body: After successful evaluation, the applicant deposits the annual licence fee plus the minimum marking fee specified for the product (as per Annexure I of Scheme-I of the BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018, as amended). The licence permits use of the ISI Standard Mark for the varieties covered under its granted scope. Fee: Annual licence fee: Rs. 1,000 plus product-specific minimum marking fee

chunks.title: ISI Mark - Product Certification (Scheme-I): Average time to grant of licence
chunks.body: Average time for grant of licence under Option-2 (existing acceptable test report) is generally about one month; under Option-1 (BIS-arranged testing) it is generally about four months from receipt of a complete application. Actual time may vary due to query responses, scheduling of inspection(s), sample deposition and fee payment. Time: Option-2: ~1 month; Option-1: ~4 months (from date of complete application)

chunks.title: ISI Mark - Product Certification (Scheme-I): Validity and renewal of licence
chunks.body: Certification under Scheme-I may initially be granted for up to two years and covers only the varieties mentioned in the licence. On renewal, the licence may be extended for up to five years from the last date of validity, subject to application with requisite fee and documents. Time: Initial validity: up to 2 years; renewable up to 5 years

chunks.title: ISI Mark - Product Certification (Scheme-I): Ongoing surveillance after licence grant
chunks.body: BIS carries out surprise factory surveillance inspections (through BIS officers or appointed agents) to verify continued conformity, and also carries out market surveillance by purchasing ISI-marked product samples for third-party lab testing.

chunks.title: FMCS (Foreign Manufacturers Certification Scheme): Nominate an Authorised Indian Representative (AIR)
chunks.body: A foreign manufacturer seeking an ISI mark for export to India must nominate an Authorised Indian Representative, a registered Indian entity or resident who handles communication with BIS on the manufacturer's behalf; an AIR normally represents only one foreign manufacturer.

chunks.title: FMCS (Foreign Manufacturers Certification Scheme): Apply online and undergo assessment
chunks.body: Application, factory assessment and testing follow a process broadly similar to the domestic Scheme-I product certification route, coordinated through the AIR.

chunks.title: Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS): Confirm the product is covered by a notified CRO/QCO
chunks.body: CRS applies only to products specifically notified under an order such as the Electronics and IT Goods (Requirements for Compulsory Registration) Order, 2012, or the MNRE Solar Photovoltaics order of 2017 - not to all electronics or solar products generally.

chunks.title: Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS): Test at a BIS-recognised lab and apply for registration
chunks.body: Manufacturers must have the product tested at a BIS-recognised laboratory and then apply for registration through the CRS portal; registration is granted per manufacturer/factory location, brand and model.

chunks.title: Hallmarking: Register online with BIS
chunks.body: Any jeweller wishing to sell hallmarked gold/silver jewellery or artefacts applies online on the BIS portal (manakonline.in). The certificate of registration is granted instantly, without needing to upload documents or pay any fee. Fee: No fee for jeweller registration Time: Instant (online, on submission)

chunks.title: Hallmarking: Approach a BIS-recognised Assaying & Hallmarking Centre (AHC)
chunks.body: A consumer can get their own jewellery/sample tested at any BIS-recognised Assaying & Hallmarking Centre, on a chargeable basis; the AHC issues an Assay Report against the identifications marked on the article. Fee: Chargeable (testing charge set by the AHC)

chunks.title: Gold 22 Carat 22K 916
chunks.body: BIS Standard Mark (BIS logo); purity of the article in caratage and fineness; six-digit alphanumeric HUID number Confirms third-party assurance that the article's actual gold purity matches what is marked, i.e. 91.6% pure gold HUID (Hallmark Unique Identification) is a six-digit alphanumeric number, unique and traceable for each hallmarked item, introduced with effect from 1 July 2021 Verify the HUID number using the 'Verify HUID' feature in the official BIS CARE mobile application Each article in a pair, and all detachable parts, must carry hallmarking with different HUIDs; check hallmarking and fineness details on each piece separately

chunks.title: Gold 18 Carat 18K 750
chunks.body: BIS Standard Mark (BIS logo); purity of the article in caratage and fineness; six-digit alphanumeric HUID number Confirms third-party assurance that the article's actual gold purity matches what is marked, i.e. 75.0% pure gold HUID (Hallmark Unique Identification) is a six-digit alphanumeric number, unique and traceable for each hallmarked item, introduced with effect from 1 July 2021 Verify the HUID number using the 'Verify HUID' feature in the official BIS CARE mobile application Each article in a pair, and all detachable parts, must carry hallmarking with different HUIDs; check hallmarking and fineness details on each piece separately

chunks.title: Gold 14 Carat 14K 585
chunks.body: BIS Standard Mark (BIS logo); purity of the article in caratage and fineness; six-digit alphanumeric HUID number Confirms third-party assurance that the article's actual gold purity matches what is marked, i.e. 58.5% pure gold HUID (Hallmark Unique Identification) is a six-digit alphanumeric number, unique and traceable for each hallmarked item, introduced with effect from 1 July 2021 Verify the HUID number using the 'Verify HUID' feature in the official BIS CARE mobile application Each article in a pair, and all detachable parts, must carry hallmarking with different HUIDs; check hallmarking and fineness details on each piece separately

chunks.title: Gold / Silver
chunks.body: Objective of the Hallmarking Scheme Hallmarking is the accurate determination and official recording of the proportionate content of precious metal in an article, to protect the public against adulteration and obligate manufacturers to maintain legal standards of fineness. Currently, gold and silver are the two precious metals covered under BIS Hallmarking.

chunks.title: Gold / Silver
chunks.body: Consumer compensation for purity shortfall If hallmarked jewellery bought by a consumer is found to be of lower purity than marked, the buyer is entitled to compensation equal to two times the value of the purity shortfall (calculated on the weight of the article), plus reimbursement of testing charges. Get the article re-tested at a BIS-recognised Assaying & Hallmarking Centre Preserve the original hallmarking documentation and purchase invoice

chunks.title: Gold / Silver
chunks.body: Mandatory marks on hallmarked jewellery (jeweller obligations) Under the mandatory hallmarking system, the following marks are compulsory on hallmarked jewellery: (i) BIS Standard Mark/BIS logo, (ii) Purity in carat and fineness, (iii) Six-digit HUID number. The manufacturer or jeweller may additionally put their own mark on the item. Only BIS registered/certified jewellers can approach an Assaying & Hallmarking Centre for hallmarking jewellery on behalf of a customer

chunks.title: What is a BIS product certification licence?
chunks.body: A licence is granted under Section 13 of the BIS Act 2016 to use a specified Standard Mark on goods that conform to the relevant Indian Standard.

chunks.title: For which products is a BIS licence compulsory?
chunks.body: Products are brought under compulsory certification by the Central Government under the BIS Act, 2016 or other applicable Acts, through Quality Control Orders. The current list of products covered is published on the official Products under Compulsory Certification page.

chunks.title: What is the fee for a BIS product certification licence?
chunks.body: An application fee of Rs. 1,000 is payable with the application. An inspection fee of Rs. 7,000 per man-day is payable before the preliminary inspection visit. On grant of the licence, an annual licence fee of Rs. 1,000 plus the product-specific minimum marking fee (per Annexure I of Scheme-I of the BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018, as amended) is payable.

chunks.title: What is the timeline for grant of a BIS product certification licence?
chunks.body: Average time for grant of licence under Option-2 (existing acceptable test report) is generally about one month; under Option-1 (BIS-arranged testing) it is generally about four months from the date of receipt of a complete application, subject to variation for reasons like query response delays, inspection scheduling, sample deposition and fee payment.

chunks.title: What is the validity of a BIS product certification licence?
chunks.body: Certification under Scheme-I may initially be granted for up to two years, valid only for the varieties mentioned in the licence, and may be renewed for up to five years from the last date of validity on application with the requisite fee and documents.

chunks.title: Can one BIS licence cover all varieties of a product made in the same factory?
chunks.body: No. A licence is granted for one product/one Indian Standard, and only covers the varieties/grades/sizes specified in the 'Scope of licence' granted; the scope can be changed (inclusion or deletion of varieties) through the applicable BIS guideline for change in scope.

chunks.title: What does a BIS Hallmark consist of?
chunks.body: Since the introduction of HUID on 1 July 2021, a hallmark consists of three marks: the BIS logo (Standard Mark), the purity of the article in caratage and fineness, and a six-digit alphanumeric HUID number.

chunks.title: How can a consumer verify a HUID number?
chunks.body: The HUID number can be verified using the 'Verify HUID' feature in the official BIS CARE mobile application.

chunks.title: What compensation is a consumer entitled to if hallmarked jewellery purity is found lower than marked?
chunks.body: The buyer is entitled to compensation equal to two times the value of the purity shortfall (calculated on the weight of the article sold), plus reimbursement of the testing charges.

chunks.title: How does BIS record and act on consumer complaints?
chunks.body: BIS follows a well-established complaint redressal procedure. Complaints are recorded centrally at the Complaints Management and Enforcement Department (CMED); complaints can be made offline or online, through the BIS CARE mobile app or the Standard Promotion Portal; on receipt, the complaint is investigated and further action taken for redressal.

chunks.title: Is BIS certification mandatory or voluntary?
chunks.body: BIS certification is basically voluntary. However, for a number of products, compliance with Indian Standards is made compulsory by the Central Government - considering public interest, protection of human/animal/plant health, environmental safety, prevention of unfair trade practices, or national security - through the issuance of Quality Control Orders (QCOs) that mandate use of the Standard Mark under a Licence or Certificate of Conformity.

chunks.title: BIS kya hai?
chunks.body: Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) India ka National Standards Body hai, BIS Act 2016 ke under. Yeh products, processes aur services ke liye Indian Standards banata hai, aur Product Certification, System Certification, Hallmarking, aur Compulsory Registration jaisi schemes chalata hai. Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution ke under aata hai. Isse pehle yeh Indian Standards Institution (ISI) ke naam se 1947 se kaam kar raha tha.

chunks.title: BIS aur ISO mein kya fark hai?
chunks.body: BIS India ka apna national standards body hai jo Indian Standards banata aur certify karta hai. ISO (International Organization for Standardization) ek global body hai jo international standards banata hai. BIS India ki taraf se ISO me participate karta hai aur kayi Indian Standards ISO standards ke saath harmonize/adopt kiye jaate hain (isliye kai IS numbers ke saath corresponding ISO number bhi likha milta hai, jaise is CSV me dikh raha hai).

chunks.title: Standard aur certification mein difference?
chunks.body: Standard (IS number) ek document hai jo batata hai product/process kaise design, test, ya manufacture hona chahiye. Certification woh process hai jisse BIS verify karta hai ki tumhara actual product us standard ko follow karta hai - tab jaake ISI mark ya registration milta hai.

chunks.title: BIS CARE app kaise use karu?
chunks.body: Play Store/App Store se free download karo, mobile number se OTP register karo, phir product par likha license/HUID/R-number daal ke authenticity verify karo. Complaints file karne ke liye 'Complaints' section use karo. App me BIS labs, offices, aur standards ki info bhi milti hai.

chunks.title: Free mein standards kaise dekhu?
chunks.body: Jo standards Quality Control Orders (mandatory certification) ke under aate hain, unhe BIS free-of-cost view/download karne deta hai. Baaki (voluntary) standards ke liye official e-Sale portal (standardsbis.bsbedge.com) se kharidna padta hai - price standard ke hisaab se alag hota hai.

chunks.title: ISI mark mandatory hai ya voluntary?
chunks.body: By default BIS certification voluntary hai. Lekin jo products government ke Quality Control Order (QCO) list me notify ho chuke hain (jaise cement, steel, toys, helmets, packaged drinking water, electronics ke kai items), unke liye ISI mark/CRS registration LEGALLY MANDATORY hai - bina certification bechna BIS Act 2016 ke under punishable hai.

chunks.title: License kitne saal ke liye valid hota hai?
chunks.body: Normally 1 saal, phir annual renewal karna padta hai (fee + surveillance visit ke saath).

chunks.title: What is BIS — Bureau of Indian Standards
chunks.body: BIS is the National Standards Body of India. It works on Indian Standards, marking and quality certification under the BIS Act, 2016 and the BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018. Services include Know Your Standard, Scheme-I ISI licences, Scheme-II CRS, FMCS, hallmarking, laboratory recognition, management-system certification, training, Standards Clubs and consumer complaints.

chunks.title: BIS Act, Rules and Regulations
chunks.body: Public documents include BIS Act 2016, BIS Rules 2018, Conformity Assessment Regulations 2018 (and later amendments), and Hallmarking Regulations 2018. Always open the live Act/Rules page for the current PDF.

chunks.title: Scheme-I ISI Mark product certification
chunks.body: Licence-based product certification. Typical flow on Manakonline: find the Indian Standard, apply, inspection, testing in a BIS/recognised lab, grant of licence, use of ISI Standard Mark with CM/L licence number. Used for many QCO-notified products and voluntary licences.

chunks.title: Scheme-II Compulsory Registration Scheme CRS
chunks.body: Registration based on self-declaration of conformity plus a test report from a BIS-recognised lab. Typical CRS grant does not include factory inspection. Mark is the CRS Standard Mark with unique R-number. Portal: crsbis.in.

chunks.title: FMCS Foreign Manufacturers Certification Scheme
chunks.body: Overseas factories placing regulated goods on the Indian market apply through FMCS, appoint an Authorized Indian Representative, and complete inspection/testing as prescribed before using the licensed Standard Mark.

chunks.title: Know Your Standard portal
chunks.body: Official search by IS number or product keyword. Shows metadata, amendments, linked licences and labs. Full standard PDF follows the official download/login path. Catalogue rows in this assistant are metadata (id + title), not full clause text.

chunks.title: BIS Care App consumer verification
chunks.body: Consumers can verify ISI licence numbers, CRS registrations and jewellery HUID through official BIS digital services / BIS Care App rather than trusting a shop claim alone.

chunks.title: CRS legal basis Scheme-II
chunks.body: CRS grant and operation follow Scheme-II of Schedule-II of the BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018. Electronics/IT coverage started with the Electronics and Information Technology Goods (Requirement for Compulsory Registration) Order, 2012 (MeitY, 03 Oct 2012). Later additions cover more electronics, MNRE solar PV goods (2017), some chemicals, and cotton bales. Ministries: MeitY, MNRE, Chemicals and Fertilizers, Textiles.

chunks.title: Who must comply with CRS
chunks.body: The manufacturer (factory owner) of a product under a Compulsory Registration Order. The Orders say no person shall manufacture or store for sale, import, sell or distribute such goods unless they conform to the specified Indian Standard and bear the Standard Mark with a unique BIS registration number (R-number).

chunks.title: Official CRS registration steps
chunks.body: 1 Generate Test Request on crsbis.in and select a BIS-recognised lab. 2 Send sample plus Test Request to the lab within 60 days of generating the Test Request. 3 Get the product tested against the notified Indian Standard. 4 Verify the lab test report. 5 Apply on the portal using that verified test report within 90 days of its issue. 6 Upload checklist documents (business licence in English or certified translation, brand papers, Form-I; foreign applicants add AIR nomination). 7 On grant, mark each product/pack with the CRS Standard Mark and unique R-number.

chunks.title: CRS Standard Mark versus ISI mark
chunks.body: CRS goods carry the Scheme-II Standard Mark plus unique R-number. Scheme-I ISI uses the ISI mark plus CM/L licence number on Manakonline. Do not mix the two marks. A product is under one notified route unless official text says otherwise. ISO 9001 factory certificates are not a substitute for CRS or ISI where a QCO applies.

chunks.title: Where to read the live CRS product list
chunks.body: The notified product + Indian Standard + QCO date table is on the official CRS products page. Always re-check the live page before telling a user a product is or is not notified.

chunks.title: How ISO and IEC standards become Indian Standards
chunks.body: BIS may adopt an international standard as an Indian Standard. Identical adoptions are commonly shown with dual numbering (IS number and ISO/IEC number) or as IS/ISO or IS/IEC. Modified adoptions are marked MOD / technically equivalent on committee lists. Confirm degree of equivalence on Know Your Standard.

chunks.title: Common IS/ISO management system standards used in India
chunks.body: Widely used adoptions include IS/ISO 9001 quality management, IS/ISO 14001 environmental management, IS/ISO 45001 occupational health and safety, IS/ISO 22000 food safety, IS/ISO 50001 energy management, IS/ISO 13485 medical devices QMS, IS/ISO 39001 road traffic safety, IS/ISO 21101 adventure tourism safety, IS 15700 service quality (SQMS), IS 15000 HACCP. These are Indian Standard designations of the international documents as adopted by BIS.

chunks.title: An ISO certificate is not an ISI or CRS licence
chunks.body: An ISO 9001 certificate from a certification body is not the same as a BIS Scheme-I licence or Scheme-II CRS registration. QCO-notified products still need the notified BIS route even if the factory already holds ISO management-system certification.
